title: Java EL Injection WAF Bypass via Reflection and Method Signature Strings
vuln_pattern: Expression Language (EL) injection in a Java web application parameter (e.g., country validator) leading to remote code execution, with a WAF filtering common keywords for SQLi, XSS, OS injection, code injection, and Java classes/methods.
fingerprint: Java web application with user input passed to an Expression Language evaluator
Input field named 'country' or similar validator endpoint
WAF blocking strings: ", ', #, >, <, bash, &, |, ;, `, ~, *, for, while, goto, if, Runtime, class, java, Name, char, Process, cmd, eval, Char, true, false, +, -, /, *, %, 0-9
Error messages or behavior indicating EL evaluation
exploit_steps: Identify the EL injection point (e.g., a parameter in a country validation endpoint that reflects evaluated input).
Determine the WAF filter rules (case-sensitive blocklist of SQLi, XSS, OS injection, code injection, Java injection, and numeric characters).
Obtain a reference to java.lang.Class without using the blocked strings, e.g., via `[].getClass().getClass()` which does not contain any filtered keywords.

Use reflection on the Class object to obtain java.lang.Runtime without naming it directly: retrieve the `forName` method and invoke it with a string argument that bypasses the numeric filter by constructing strings from method signatures (e.g., calling `toString()` on a method reference).
Construct the command execution chain: get the `exec` method from Runtime's class, and invoke it with the desired OS command string built similarly from method-signature-to-string conversions.
Exfiltrate command output via DNS/HTTP callbacks or reflected output if possible, using similar string-construction techniques.
key_payloads: forName method invoked with a non-numeric string built from method signature conversion
getRuntime() obtained through reflection without using 'Runtime' literal
exec() with command string constructed from method signature strings
